exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form

question.text: The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $B?$ \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1\\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $2$ pivots in the $1$st and $3$rd columns:

\[ B= \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} B &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_2&:=R_2+(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_3&:=R_3+2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 &\bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & 2 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{4} & 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\\ 0 & 1& 1 & 4 & -5\\ 4 & 0 & 3 & -6 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} B &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 & -5\\ 4 & 0 & 3 & -6 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_3&:=R_3+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 1 & 4 & -5\\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{5} & -8 & -3\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{7} & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $4$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $4.$

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $C,$ given by \[ C=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & 8 & 0 & -2\\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ \end{bmatrix}. \]

First, we need to convert $C$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} C &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & 8 & 0 & -2\\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix} & R_3&:=R_3+\dfrac 1 2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 2 & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{8} & 0 & -2\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & -1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $C$ has $4$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $4.$

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $Q,$ given by \[ Q=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 3\\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 8 & -12\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $Q$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} Q &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 3\\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 8 & -12\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_4&:=R_4+\dfrac 1 4R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} & 1 & 1 & 0 & 3\\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & -1 & 1 & 4\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{8} & -12\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $Q$ has $4$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $4.$

example.title: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $D,$ given by \[ D=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & -3& 0 &0 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 2 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -2 &-8 & 7 \\ 0 &0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $D$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} D &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & -3& 0 &0 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 2 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & -2 &-8 & 7 \\ 0 &0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} & R_4&:=R_4+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & -3& 0 &0 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 2 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 & 7 \\ 0 &0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} & R_4&:=R_4+\left(\dfrac{2}{7}\right)R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-3}& 0 &0 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{4} &2 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 &\bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-7} & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 &\bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $D$ has $5$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $5.$

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &R_2&\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by \[ A= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} &R_1&\leftrightarrow R_4 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &R_3&:= R_3 + \dfrac{1}{2}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{4} & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.

example.title: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} P &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3 \end{bmatrix} &R_3&:= R_3 + 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 & -3 \end{bmatrix} &R_4&:= R_4 + 2R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-1} & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 0 & 9 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $4$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $2$nd, $3$rd, $5$th, and $6$th columns.

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -6 & 0 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -8 & 0 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} P &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -6 & 0 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -8 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &R_3&:= R_3 + 2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 8 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -8 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &R_4&:= R_4 + R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{8} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $4$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $2$nd, $3$rd, $5$th and $6$th columns.
